c.st: Dandelion Root Recipes
c.x:
My father grew up fairly poor in the 1930s and they often were short on food but he said they always had vegetables. They harvested dandelions, ate them, and actually made dandelion wine (according to him).

He and his siblings loved vegetables as during certain times of the year they were the one thing they had "too much of". Everything else was basically rationed but they would get various peak harvests where they could eat until they were full.

And you could set the environmental variables to be as precise as you need. If you need 29 digits of precision, you can quickly show that you know 1.4142135623730950488016887242 and nothing more.

A reasonable metaphor would be that you cannot draw all of the Mandelbrot diagram, but you can render any piece of it to any resolution you choose. Being able to describe it precisely, and to know the limits of your accuracy, is useful.
